definition: using something as the starting point or evidence
example: Our forecast is based on last quarter's data.
exampleEs: Nuestro pronóstico se basa en los datos del trimestre pasado.
cloze: Our forecast is based ____ last quarter's data.
note: You said 'based in this paragraph' before. Use 'on'. 'Based in' is only for a place: 'a company based in Austin'.

definition: to be decided or affected by something
example: Whether we ship on Friday depends on the QA results.
exampleEs: Que lancemos el viernes depende de los resultados de QA.
cloze: Whether we ship on Friday depends ____ the QA results.
note: Spanish 'depender de' tempts you to say 'depend of'. In English it is always 'on'.

definition: wanting to learn more about something
example: I'm really interested in how language models handle long context.
exampleEs: Me interesa mucho cómo los modelos de lenguaje manejan el contexto largo.
cloze: I'm really interested ____ how language models handle long context.
note: 'Interested about' is a common mistake. Use 'in'.

definition: skilled when doing something
example: She is really good at debugging race conditions.
exampleEs: Ella es muy buena depurando condiciones de carrera.
cloze: She is really good ____ debugging race conditions.
note: Use 'good at' for skills. 'Good with' is for handling people or tools: 'good with kids'.

definition: having the duty to take care of something
example: Who is responsible for the deployment pipeline?
exampleEs: ¿Quién es responsable del pipeline de despliegue?
cloze: Who is responsible ____ the deployment pipeline?
note: Spanish 'responsable de' becomes 'responsible for', not 'of'.

definition: being the person who controls or manages something
example: Maria is in charge of the onboarding project.
exampleEs: María está a cargo del proyecto de incorporación.
cloze: Maria is in charge ____ the onboarding project.
note: Say 'in charge of', not 'in charge for'. Compare: 'responsible for'.

definition: right now
example: I can't talk because I'm in a meeting at the moment.
exampleEs: No puedo hablar porque estoy en una reunión en este momento.
cloze: I can't talk because I'm in a meeting ____ the moment.
note: You said 'in this time'. Use 'at the moment' or 'at this time' for right now.

definition: at exactly the planned time, not late
example: The train left on time, so we arrived early.
exampleEs: El tren salió a tiempo, así que llegamos temprano.
cloze: The train left ____ time, so we arrived early.
note: 'On time' means punctual. 'In time' means early enough to do something.

definition: early enough to do something before it is too late
example: We finished the patch just in time for the release.
exampleEs: Terminamos el parche justo a tiempo para el lanzamiento.
cloze: We finished the patch just ____ time for the release.
collocations: in time to catch the bus
note: 'In time for' + event: early enough for it. 'On time': exactly at the scheduled moment.

definition: to reach a specific place or event
example: We arrived at the venue ten minutes early.
exampleEs: Llegamos al lugar diez minutos antes.
cloze: We arrived ____ the venue ten minutes early.
note: Never 'arrive to'. Use 'at' for a specific point (airport, hotel, office).

definition: to reach a city, country or large area
example: Our flight arrives in Boston at noon.
exampleEs: Nuestro vuelo llega a Boston al mediodía.
cloze: Our flight arrives ____ Boston at noon.
note: Use 'in' for cities and countries, 'at' for specific places like an airport.

definition: to discuss a topic
example: Let's talk about the roadmap before the call ends.
exampleEs: Hablemos del roadmap antes de que termine la llamada.
cloze: Let's talk ____ the roadmap before the call ends.
note: The verb 'discuss' takes no preposition ('discuss the plan'), but 'talk' needs 'about'.

definition: to pay attention to a sound or a person
example: I listen to podcasts while I code.
exampleEs: Escucho podcasts mientras programo.
cloze: I listen ____ podcasts while I code.
note: Spanish 'escuchar' has no preposition, but English 'listen' always needs 'to'.

definition: having someone as your husband or wife
example: My manager has been married to her college friend for ten years.
exampleEs: Mi jefa lleva diez años casada con su amiga de la universidad.
cloze: My manager has been married ____ her college friend for ten years.
note: Spanish says 'casado con', but English uses 'married to'. 'Married with' only appears with children: 'married with two kids'.

definition: to be made up of certain parts
example: The team consists of six engineers and two designers.
exampleEs: El equipo está formado por seis ingenieros y dos diseñadores.
cloze: The team consists ____ six engineers and two designers.
note: Not used in the continuous form: say 'consists of', not 'is consisting of'.

es: en cuanto a, en términos de
definition: used to say which aspect you are talking about
example: In terms of cost, option B is much cheaper.
exampleEs: En términos de costo, la opción B es mucho más barata.
cloze: In terms ____ cost, option B is much cheaper.
note: A useful linker for meetings. The whole phrase is fixed: 'in terms of'.

definition: not later than the end of a period
example: I'll send the report by the end of the week.
exampleEs: Enviaré el informe a más tardar a fin de semana.
cloze: I'll send the report by the end ____ the week.
collocations: by the end of the day
by the end of the year
by the end of the meeting
note: 'By' means 'not later than'. 'At the end of' means exactly at that point.

definition: to feel happy about something that will happen
example: I look forward to working with your team.
exampleEs: Espero con ganas trabajar con tu equipo.
cloze: I look forward ____ working with your team.
note: After 'to' here comes an -ing form: 'look forward to hearing from you', not 'to hear'.

definition: feeling anxious about a problem
example: I'm worried about the deadline for the demo.
exampleEs: Me preocupa la fecha límite de la demostración.
cloze: I'm worried ____ the deadline for the demo.
note: Use 'worried about' for the cause of worry.

definition: feeling fear because of something
example: Many people are afraid of losing their jobs to AI.
exampleEs: Mucha gente tiene miedo de perder su trabajo por la IA.
cloze: Many people are afraid ____ losing their jobs to AI.
note: Spanish 'miedo de' maps directly to 'afraid of'.

definition: not the same as something else
example: Version 2 is very different from version 1.
exampleEs: La versión 2 es muy diferente de la versión 1.
cloze: Version 2 is very different ____ version 1.
note: American English also accepts 'different than'. Avoid 'different of'.

definition: almost the same as something
example: Our approach is similar to what the paper describes.
exampleEs: Nuestro enfoque es similar al que describe el artículo.
cloze: Our approach is similar ____ what the paper describes.
note: Not 'similar with'. Use 'similar to'.

definition: to direct your eyes or attention to something
example: Can you look at this pull request when you have a minute?
exampleEs: ¿Puedes mirar este pull request cuando tengas un minuto?
cloze: Can you look ____ this pull request when you have a minute?
note: 'Look at' is to direct your eyes; 'look for' is to search.

definition: to try to find something
example: I'm looking for a good Minecraft server to join.
exampleEs: Estoy buscando un buen servidor de Minecraft al cual unirme.
cloze: I'm looking ____ a good Minecraft server to join.
note: Spanish 'buscar' has no preposition, but English 'look' needs 'for'.

definition: to stay until something happens or someone arrives
example: We're waiting for approval from the legal team.
exampleEs: Estamos esperando la aprobación del equipo legal.
cloze: We're waiting ____ approval from the legal team.
note: 'Wait for' takes the thing or person you expect. Don't say 'wait to' + noun.

definition: to give money in exchange for something
example: Who's paying for the new server?
exampleEs: ¿Quién paga el servidor nuevo?
cloze: Who's paying ____ the new server?
note: You pay a person ('pay him') but pay for a thing ('pay for the licence').

definition: to use money or time for something
example: We spent two weeks on the migration.
exampleEs: Dedicamos dos semanas a la migración.
cloze: We spent two weeks ____ the migration.
note: Also correct: 'spend two weeks migrating' with an -ing form and no preposition.

definition: to have the same opinion as someone
example: I agree with you on that point.
exampleEs: Estoy de acuerdo contigo en ese punto.
cloze: I agree ____ you on that point.
note: Don't say 'I am agree'. It is 'I agree', with no 'am'.

definition: to decide something together
example: The team agreed on a release date after a long discussion.
exampleEs: El equipo acordó una fecha de lanzamiento tras una larga discusión.
cloze: The team agreed ____ a release date after a long discussion.
note: 'Agree with' is for a person or opinion; 'agree on' is for a decision.

definition: to formally ask for a job or position
example: She applied for a position at a startup in Berlin.
exampleEs: Ella solicitó un puesto en una startup en Berlín.
cloze: She applied ____ a position at a startup in Berlin.
note: You apply FOR the job and TO the company.

definition: to be owned by or a member of something
example: This server belongs to a community of Minecraft fans.
exampleEs: Este servidor pertenece a una comunidad de fans de Minecraft.
cloze: This server belongs ____ a community of Minecraft fans.
note: 'Belong' is never used in the continuous form.

definition: to have an illness or a problem
example: Many developers suffer from burnout.
exampleEs: Muchos desarrolladores sufren de agotamiento.
cloze: Many developers suffer ____ burnout.
note: Spanish 'sufrir de' becomes 'suffer from'.

definition: to give your attention to one thing
example: Let's focus on the user's problem first.
exampleEs: Enfoquémonos primero en el problema del usuario.
cloze: Let's focus ____ the user's problem first.
note: Useful for ADHD-friendly goals: 'focus on one thing at a time'.

definition: to need or trust someone or something
example: We rely on automated tests to catch regressions.
exampleEs: Dependemos de pruebas automatizadas para detectar regresiones.
cloze: We rely ____ automated tests to catch regressions.
note: Similar to 'depend on'; both always take 'on'.

definition: to demand something firmly
example: He insisted on reviewing every change himself.
exampleEs: Insistió en revisar cada cambio él mismo.
cloze: He insisted ____ reviewing every change himself.
note: Spanish 'insistir en' maps directly to 'insist on'.

definition: to achieve what you were trying to do
example: We succeeded in reducing the latency by half.
exampleEs: Logramos reducir la latencia a la mitad.
cloze: We succeeded ____ reducing the latency by half.
note: Followed by an -ing form: 'succeeded in finishing', not 'succeeded to finish'.

definition: feeling pleased about an achievement
example: I'm proud of what the team shipped this month.
exampleEs: Estoy orgulloso de lo que el equipo entregó este mes.
cloze: I'm proud ____ what the team shipped this month.
note: Spanish 'orgulloso de' maps directly to 'proud of'.

definition: happy and eager about something
example: I'm excited about the new feature we're building.
exampleEs: Estoy emocionado por la nueva función que estamos construyendo.
cloze: I'm excited ____ the new feature we're building.
note: 'Excited about' is the safe choice for work conversations.

definition: bored or annoyed by something that repeats
example: I'm tired of fixing the same bug every week.
exampleEs: Estoy harto de arreglar el mismo bug cada semana.
cloze: I'm tired ____ fixing the same bug every week.
note: 'Tired of' = annoyed by. 'Tired from' = physically tired because of an activity.

definition: deliberately, not by accident
example: He didn't break it on purpose; it was an accident.
exampleEs: No lo rompió a propósito; fue un accidente.
cloze: He didn't break it ____ purpose; it was an accident.
note: The opposite is 'by accident' or 'by mistake'.

definition: without meaning to, because of an error
example: I deleted the file by mistake and had to restore it.
exampleEs: Borré el archivo por error y tuve que restaurarlo.
cloze: I deleted the file ____ mistake and had to restore it.
note: Equivalent: 'by accident'. Don't say 'in mistake'.

definition: needing to do something quickly
example: Sorry, I can't chat now because I'm in a hurry.
exampleEs: Perdón, no puedo platicar ahora porque tengo prisa.
cloze: Sorry, I can't chat now because I'm ____ a hurry.
note: Spanish says 'tener prisa', but English uses the structure 'be in a hurry'.

definition: before something happens
example: Please send the agenda in advance so we can prepare.
exampleEs: Por favor envía la agenda con anticipación para que podamos prepararnos.
cloze: Please send the agenda ____ advance so we can prepare.
note: Not 'with anticipation'. Say 'in advance'.

definition: using a phone call to talk
example: He's on the phone with the vendor right now.
exampleEs: Está al teléfono con el proveedor ahora mismo.
cloze: He's ____ the phone with the vendor right now.
note: Also 'on a call', 'on a video call', 'on Zoom'.

definition: not less than
example: We need at least three reviewers for this pull request.
exampleEs: Necesitamos al menos tres revisores para este pull request.
cloze: We need ____ least three reviewers for this pull request.
note: 'At least' is also a discourse marker: 'At least it works'.

definition: used to say what you personally think
example: In my opinion, the old design was cleaner.
exampleEs: En mi opinión, el diseño anterior era más limpio.
cloze: ____ my opinion, the old design was cleaner.
note: Not 'for my opinion' or 'on my opinion'. Use 'in my opinion' or 'in my view'.

definition: used to introduce a contrasting point
example: The cloud option is faster. On the other hand, it costs more.
exampleEs: La opción en la nube es más rápida. Por otro lado, cuesta más.
cloze: The cloud option is faster. ____ the other hand, it costs more.
note: Often paired with 'on the one hand' at the start.

definition: in the beginning, before things changed
example: At first I didn't understand the question.
exampleEs: Al principio no entendí la pregunta.
cloze: ____ first I didn't understand the question.
note: 'At first' implies that things changed later. Don't confuse with 'first' as in 'first of all'.

definition: after a long process, finally
example: We tried three tools, and in the end we built our own.
exampleEs: Probamos tres herramientas y al final construimos la nuestra.
cloze: We tried three tools, and ____ the end we built our own.
note: 'In the end' = finally. 'At the end of' needs an 'of' phrase.

definition: at the last part or point of something
example: The bug appeared at the end of the sprint.
exampleEs: El bug apareció al final del sprint.
cloze: The bug appeared ____ the end of the sprint.
collocations: at the end of the day
at the end of the call
at the end of the month
note: 'At the end of' is a point in time. 'By the end of' means 'not later than'.

definition: during the night
example: I do my best coding at night when it's quiet.
exampleEs: Programo mejor de noche, cuando hay silencio.
cloze: I do my best coding ____ night when it's quiet.
note: We say 'in the morning/afternoon/evening' but 'at night'.

definition: to have a friendly relationship with someone
example: I get along really well with my teammates.
exampleEs: Me llevo muy bien con mis compañeros.
cloze: I get along really well ____ my teammates.
note: British English often uses 'get on with'.

definition: to be involved in an activity
example: Everyone can take part in the discussion.
exampleEs: Todos pueden participar en la discusión.
cloze: Everyone can take part ____ the discussion.
note: 'Participate in' means the same and also takes 'in'.

definition: to say someone did something wrong
example: They accused him of cheating in the tournament.
exampleEs: Lo acusaron de hacer trampa en el torneo.
cloze: They accused him ____ cheating in the tournament.
note: Spanish 'acusar de' maps directly to 'accuse of'. Followed by an -ing form.

definition: used to thank someone for something
example: Thanks for joining the call on short notice.
exampleEs: Gracias por unirte a la llamada con tan poca anticipación.
cloze: Thanks ____ joining the call on short notice.
note: After 'for' use a noun or an -ing form: 'thanks for helping'.

definition: to make something clear to someone
example: Can you explain this to me in simpler words?
exampleEs: ¿Me lo puedes explicar con palabras más simples?
cloze: Can you explain this ____ me in simpler words?
note: Don't say 'explain me'. The person comes after 'to': 'explain it to me'.

definition: to answer a message
example: I need to reply to his email before lunch.
exampleEs: Necesito responder su correo antes de almorzar.
cloze: I need to reply ____ his email before lunch.
note: As a noun: 'a reply to your message'.

definition: to cause a particular outcome
example: That change could result in a few minutes of downtime.
exampleEs: Ese cambio podría provocar unos minutos de inactividad.
cloze: That change could result ____ a few minutes of downtime.
note: 'Result from' is the reverse: the cause. 'Delays result from bugs'.

definition: to stop something from happening
example: The rules prevent bots from spamming the channel.
exampleEs: Las reglas impiden que los bots hagan spam en el canal.
cloze: The rules prevent bots ____ spamming the channel.
note: Pattern: prevent + person + from + -ing.

definition: to laugh in order to make fun of someone
example: Don't laugh at my pronunciation, please.
exampleEs: No te rías de mi pronunciación, por favor.
cloze: Don't laugh ____ my pronunciation, please.
note: Spanish 'reírse de' becomes 'laugh at'.
